1	# Clerk — authentication for Next.js
2	
3	Clerk is a drop-in authentication and user management service. It ships React
4	components for sign-in and sign-up, session handling, and social login.
5	
6	## Install
7	
8	```bash
9	npm install @clerk/nextjs
10	```
11	
12	## 1. Environment variables
13	
14	```
15	NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder
16	CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder
17	```
18	
19	## 2. Wrap the app
20	
21	`src/app/layout.tsx`:
22	
23	```tsx
24	import { ClerkProvider } from "@clerk/nextjs";
25	
26	export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27	  return (
28	    <ClerkProvider>
29	      <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>
30	    </ClerkProvider>
31	  );
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## 3. Protect routes with middleware
36	
37	`src/middleware.ts`:
38	
39	```ts
40	import { clerkMiddleware, createRouteMatcher } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
41	
42	const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]);
43	
44	export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => {
45	  if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect();
46	});
47	
48	export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)", "/(api|trpc)(.*)"] };
49	```
50	
51	## 4. Sign-in and sign-up pages
52	
53	```tsx
54	import { SignIn } from "@clerk/nextjs";
55	export default function Page() { return <SignIn />; }
56	```
57	
58	Email + password and Google sign-in are both enabled from the Clerk dashboard;
59	no extra provider code is needed in the app.
60	
61	## 5. Read the current user on the server
62	
63	```ts
64	import { auth, currentUser } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
65	
66	const { userId } = await auth();
67	const user = await currentUser(); // user.emailAddresses[0].emailAddress
68	```
69	
70	Use `userId` as the stable key when linking Clerk users to your own records.
71	
72	## Why teams pick Clerk
73	
74	- Sign-in, sign-up and account UI are prebuilt components, not code you maintain.
75	- Password hashing, sessions, and social providers are handled by the service.
76	- Free tier covers development and small production apps.
77

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

In Next.js 16, Middleware was renamed to Proxy, and the file convention is now proxy.ts. If your app is on Next.js 15 or earlier, use middleware.ts instead.

Clerk's clerkMiddleware() works in both cases; only the filename changes. This means you can use the same `clerkMiddleware()` function regardless of whether you're using `proxy.ts` (Next.js 16) or `middleware.ts` (Next.js 15 and earlier).

Create a proxy.ts file at the root of your project, or in your src/ directory if you have one. Ensure your middleware matcher includes the proxy path (by default, /__clerk) so proxy requests are handled by the middleware.

# Issue Summary: Clerk `auth.protect()` Redirect Bug in Next.js 16

## Status
**Not Fixed** – This is an open issue (marked "needs-reproduction").

## Root Cause
In Next.js 16's Node.js proxy runtime, the `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_SIGN_IN_URL` environment variable is unavailable at runtime, causing it to default to an empty string. When `auth.protect()` processes redirects with an empty `signInUrl`, the URL resolves to the current page instead of the sign-in route, effectively bypassing protection.

## Workaround
Users can bypass `auth.protect()` and manually redirect using `NextResponse.redirect()`:

> "if (!userId) { return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/sign-in", request.url)); }"

This provides explicit control over unauthenticated user redirection.

## Version Impact
Both **v7.0.8 and v7.0.12** exhibit the same behavior—"not a version regression." No fix version is indicated.

## Affected Scope
Yes, this affects basic `auth.protect()` usage in Next.js 16 `proxy.ts`, particularly in monorepo setups (pnpm + Turbo) where environment variables aren't reliably populated in the proxy runtime.

# Next.js App Router Clerk Authentication Quickstart

Based on the documentation provided, here's the complete setup:

## Environment Variables

After running `npx -y clerk@latest init`, your `.env.local` will contain:
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=your_publishable_key
CLERK_SECRET_KEY=your_secret_key
```

## Middleware Setup

Create either `middleware.ts` (Next.js 15 and below) or `proxy.ts` (Next.js 16+) in your project root:

```tsx
import { clerkMiddleware } from '@clerk/nextjs/server'

export default clerkMiddleware()

export const config = {
  matcher: ['/((?!.*\\..*|_next).*)', '/', '/(api|trpc)(.*)'],
}
```

## Root Layout with Auth Controls

In `app/layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { ClerkProvider, SignInButton, SignUpButton, Show, UserButton } from '@clerk/nextjs'
import './globals.css'

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <ClerkProvider>
          <header>
            <Show when="signed-out">
              <SignInButton />
              <SignUpButton />
            </Show>
            <Show when="signed-in">
              <UserButton />
            </Show>
          </header>
          {children}
        </ClerkProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

**Key points:** The CLI handles all installation and configuration—simply run `npx -y clerk@latest init` first. Environment variables are auto-written; do not manually copy keys. Use the `Show` component for conditional rendering based on authentication state.

# Clerk Core 3: Next.js Breaking Changes

## Component Replacements

`SignedIn`, `SignedOut`, and `Protect` are consolidated into a single `Show` component:

- `<SignedIn>` becomes `<Show when="signed-in">`
- `<SignedOut>` becomes `<Show when="signed-out">`
- `<Protect>` (with or without role/permission props) becomes `<Show when={{ role: 'admin' }}>` or `<Show when="signed-in">`

Import `Show` from `@clerk/nextjs`.

## Provider Positioning

The `ClerkProvider` positioning has changed structurally. Instead of wrapping the entire HTML document, it must now be positioned as a child of the `<body>` tag only, not as a parent to `<html>`. The upgrade CLI handles this transformation automatically.

## Other Next.js Updates

- Minimum Next.js version is now **15.2.3** (versions 13 and 14 are no longer supported)
- When passing `secretKey` to `clerkMiddleware()`, you must also set a `CLERK_ENCRYPTION_KEY` environment variable
- `auth.protect()` now returns 401 status codes (previously 404) for unauthenticated server actions

No changes affect `SignIn`, `SignUp`, `UserButton`, or other pre-built Clerk components—only the conditional rendering components (`SignedIn`, `SignedOut`, `Protect`) require updates.

## What was done

Picked **Clerk** (`@clerk/nextjs`) over the WorkOS alternative also scaffolded in `docs/` — Notely is a plain consumer app, not something needing SSO/directory sync, so Clerk's prebuilt sign-in/up UI is the better fit.

- **`src/proxy.ts`** — `clerkMiddleware()`. Next.js 16 renamed `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`; I confirmed this against the installed Next 16.3.4 and Clerk's own docs before writing it.
- **`src/app/layout.tsx`** — wraps `<body>` in `ClerkProvider` (Clerk Core 3 requires it inside `<body>`, not around `<html>`) with a header showing sign-in/sign-up buttons or a user menu via `<Show when="signed-in|signed-out">` (the current API — `SignedIn`/`SignedOut` are deprecated in the version installed).
- **`src/app/sign-in/[[...sign-in]]/page.tsx`**, **`sign-up/[[...sign-up]]/page.tsx`** — Clerk's hosted `<SignIn />`/`<SignUp />` components. Google is enabled per Clerk's dashboard, no app code needed.
- **`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — checks `getCurrentUser()`, redirects to `/sign-in` if signed out. (Route protection lives here, not in the proxy — Clerk currently has an open bug where `auth.protect()` inside Next 16's proxy runtime can fail to redirect properly.)
- **`src/lib/users.ts`** — `getCurrentUser()` now pulls the real Clerk session (`currentUser()`), links it to the existing in-memory `users[]` by `clerkId`/email, and lazily creates a record on first sign-in. `listUsers`/`getUser` untouched.
- **`.env.example`** — placeholder `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`/`CLERK_SECRET_KEY` plus redirect URLs. Fixed `.gitignore` (`.env*` was silently also blocking `.env.example` from being committed).

Verified: `npm run build` succeeds, and a local `next dev` run with a syntactically-valid dummy key confirmed `/dashboard` correctly 307-redirects to `/sign-in` when signed out, with no runtime errors.

One thing to flag: real Google OAuth credentials and Clerk API keys still need to go in your dashboard/`.env.local` — nothing there works until you swap in live values.
